seo.description: Step-by-step clinical guide to hair transplantation. Learn about procedure duration, pain management, shock loss, and long-term result permanence.

hero.title: The Clinical Hair Transplant Process
hero.subtitle: From initial medical evaluation to lifelong results: Procedure steps, duration, and complete recovery timeline.
hero.imageAlt: Hair Transplantation Procedure and Clinical Stages

blocks.text: The 4 Main Stages of Hair Transplantation
Hair transplantation is a micro-surgical tissue transplant performed under local anesthesia. Regardless of the clinic or technique (FUE or DHI), the medical core consists of 4 primary phases:

items: **1. Planning & Hairline Design:** Donor density is evaluated, graft numbers are calculated, and a natural hairline matching facial anatomy is designed.

**2. Local Anesthesia & Graft Extraction:** The donor area is numbed using comfortable local anesthesia. Individual hair follicles (grafts) are extracted via micromotor and stored in a nutrient-rich solution.
**3. Channel Creation (Recipient Site Preparation):** Micro-incisions aligned with natural hair growth angles (40-45 degrees) are created using Sapphire blades or DHI Choi implanter pens.
**4. Graft Implantation:** Extracted grafts are meticulously placed into recipient sites (single hair grafts for the frontal hairline, multi-hair grafts for density behind).

blocks.text: How Long Does It Take and Is It Painful?
💡 Comfort Standards: Modern needle-free local anesthesia techniques ensure a virtually painless experience during and after the procedure.

A standard hair transplant session takes between **6 to 8 hours** depending on the number of grafts. Patients can watch television, listen to music, or take breaks for meals. Thanks to targeted local anesthesia, the procedure itself is pain-free, and any mild post-op discomfort is easily managed with routine pain relievers.

items: **Days 1 to 10 (Crust Removal):** Small post-operative scabs naturally shed through specialized washes by day 10, leaving a clean scalp.
**Weeks 2 to 4 (Shock Loss):** Transplanted hair shafts temporarily shed. This is a completely normal biological phase as follicles transition into a resting state.
**Months 3 to 6 (Initial Growth):** Follicles reactivate and new permanent hair strands begin to emerge, steadily thickening each month.
**Month 12 (Final Permanent Results):** Full results appear around month 12. Because donor follicles are genetically resistant to thinning hormones, transplanted hair is permanent for life.

items.a: Yes. Hair follicles harvested from the donor area (back of the head) are genetically resistant to DHT hormones, making transplanted hair permanent.

items.q: **How soon can I return to normal daily work?**
items.a: Desk jobs and non-strenuous daily activities can be resumed within 2 to 3 days. Heavy physical exercise, swimming, and saunas should be avoided for 3 to 4 weeks.

items.q: **What is the maximum graft count in a single session?**
items.a: Depending on donor area health, the safe maximum limit in a single session ranges between 4,000 and 5,000 grafts (approx. 10,000–12,000 individual hairs).
